info.description:
Enterprise Outdoor Emergency and Trail Management System API

## Retry contract
- `429 rate-limit-exceeded`, `409 resource-busy` and `503 storage-unavailable` carry a `Retry-After` header (seconds): wait at least that long before retrying. Other 4xx are not retried unchanged (on `401` refresh the tokens first, then retry once).
- `Idempotency-Key` (required on `createBooking`, optional on `raiseSos`): generate one UUID per user action and persist it until the action gets a definitive response, also across app restarts. Every retry of the same action reuses the same key: the server answers `200` with the resource already created. A new key means a new action.

## Refresh contract
- Send at most one `refreshTokens` request at a time (e.g. Ktor `Auth` plugin, `bearer { refreshTokens { } }`).
- Each refresh token is single-use. Reusing one (for instance two parallel refreshes with the same token) is treated as token theft: the whole session is revoked and the user must log in again.
- Exception for a lost response: if the connection drops before the client reads the new pair,                         it may retry with the same refresh token within 60 seconds, as long as the new token has never                         been used; the server issues a fresh pair. Never retry a refresh automatically in any other case.

## Conditional GET
Public `GET` routes under `/api/v1/trails` and `/api/v1/pois` return an `ETag` with `Cache-Control: no-cache`: send it back in `If-None-Match` to get `304 Not Modified` without a body.

## Media upload contract
Photos go straight to object storage, never through this API. Allowed types: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp` (convert HEIC to JPEG on the device), at most 10 MB.
1. `createUploadRequest` with the exact `contentType` and `sizeBytes` of the file to send.
2. `POST` a `multipart/form-data` request to `uploadUrl`, without the bearer token: every entry of `formFields` unchanged (any order), then the `file` part **last**, with the same `Content-Type`. The request needs a `Content-Length` (no chunked encoding). Storage answers `204`; a bigger file (`400 EntityTooLarge`) or a changed field (`403`) is rejected by storage itself.
3. After the `204`, call `confirmUpload`: `READY`, or `QUARANTINED` if the content is not the declared image. `422` means storage has no file yet. `confirmUpload` can be retried and returns the same outcome.
4. The policy expires at `expiresAt` (10 minutes): after that, start again from step 1.
